resolved_findings.reason: Qualification and final-custody hash/size descriptors are prepared before one final monotonic elapsed sample. The final strict wall-cap predicate and terminal inclusive duration use that same value. A retained cap violation prevents success. Completion uses the prepared custody descriptor and performs no later descriptor hash or filesystem existence check.
resolved_findings.boundary: Declared final sample before completion classification; terminal construction, publication and return tail remain outside that sample. No whole-process hard deadline is certified.

only_runnable_delta: supervise.py final wall-cap predicate after receipt preparation
limits: Source review grants no execution, staging, scientific fitting, TEST access or predictive authority.
Syntax, importability, controlled clock boundary behavior, runtime/RNG parity, numerical parity, serialization, resources and full-graph feasibility remain unverified.
Upstream AST/compile assertions are metadata, not independently verified runtime facts.
Final classification uses one declared elapsed sample; terminal construction/publication/return tail is not included in that sample, as disclosed in v2 README and terminal_write_tail_measured=False.
Root raw-feature equality remains a reported prerequisite; its outcome receipt and feature payload were not opened.
Child PASS alone is insufficient for cap-qualified physical completion; supervisor COMPLETE and bound output custody are also required.
Output custody is an inventory of owned outputs, not an asynchronous input freeze.
Sampled session RSS can miss transients; exceptional cleanup can lack complete kernel usage, as disclosed in the preserved v1 review.
